title: Historical identifier resolution requires conjunctive agreement across five identity predicates

observed: The active queue requires M-004, M-005, and M-006 candidates to be resolved using namespace, owner, semantic role, temporal precedence, and immutable locator agreement.
The queue requires exhaustive branch or equivalent repository-history coverage before an identifier may be classified as unlocated.
CM-1026 reserves unresolved identifiers and prohibits treating them as available names.
Before this slice, the five identity predicates were not represented by a dedicated fail-closed JSON Schema contract.
inferred: The five predicates form a conjunction rather than a weighted score: failure or uncertainty in any one predicate leaves the historical identity unresolved or rejects the candidate.
Semantic similarity alone cannot compensate for namespace, ownership, chronology, or immutable-locator disagreement.
A verified result without exhaustive reproduced coverage would overstate the repository evidence.
proposed: Use operations/continuity/schemas/historical-identifier-resolution.schema.json for every future M-004, M-005, or M-006 candidate assessment.
Promote a candidate to verified only when coverage_state is exhaustive_reproduced and every predicate passes with at least one immutable evidence locator.
Retain unresolved or candidate_rejected status when any predicate is unknown or fails, and preserve the falsification route.
superseded: Resolving a historical identifier from name resemblance, suffix collision, automation prose, or semantic similarity alone.
Treating the five identity predicates as optional corroboration rather than a conjunctive identity boundary.
unresolved: No candidate for M-004, M-005, or M-006 has yet satisfied the new contract.
Exhaustive branch and history traversal remains outstanding.
The originating decision log, language lexicon, project document, or approved chat-history source remains unlocated.

source_provenance.supports: Queue ownership, priority, acceptance criteria, exhaustive-coverage requirement, and the five named identity predicates.
The reservation rule for unresolved historical identifiers.
The new machine-checkable conjunctive resolution gate.

verification.method: Inspected the exact active-queue blob and recent continuity commits, compared the new contract against prior reservation and provenance-transition work, and confirmed this slice adds the previously missing five-predicate candidate-resolution structure rather than duplicating the monotonic coverage-state record.
limitations: No JSON Schema validator was executed in this connector-only run.
No exhaustive branch inventory was available through the current connector path.
The schema defines promotion conditions but does not assert that any historical candidate is genuine.

included: repository paths and immutable commit or blob identifiers

falsification_routes: Produce an authoritative source showing that fewer than all five predicates are sufficient for identity resolution.
Validate a verified candidate with a failed or unknown predicate against the committed schema and demonstrate acceptance.
Locate an earlier authoritative executable contract that already enforced the same five-predicate conjunction.
